epistemic_purpose: repair stale live Backgrounded + Cancel projection after authoritative CommandJob terminality

verdict_history.summary: Multi-job production projection bug: the runner fired onBackgroundStateChange(false, undefined) ONLY on the >0->0 cardinal flip. When J1 terminalized while J2 stayed running, no callback fired; J1's projection stayed 'running' forever (stale Backgrounded pill). The predecessor's BCTCP-06 multi-job test manually injected the desired end state but did NOT exercise the production composition.

Bounded repair moves the per-job terminal signal UPSTREAM to the runner (carrying jobId + terminalState, NOT gated on becameIdle). Controller projection maintains the per-job map, derives the scalar from it, and computes the active taskId as the LAST running entry. BTCONT predicate fires exactly once on the >0->0 transition (the LAST running job terminalizes with taskId=undefined).

reproduction_red_001.reviewer_demand: start J1, start J2, terminalize J1 while J2 remains running; assert projection[J1]=exited AND projection[J2]=running AND backgroundCommandRunning=true
reproduction_red_001.pre_correction01_behavior: J1's terminalPromise resolves with becameIdle=false (J2 still alive); runner drops the signal via `if (becameIdle)`; projection[J1] stays 'running' forever
reproduction_red_001.post_correction01_behavior: Runner fires (false, J1, 'exited') UNCONDITIONALLY; controller updates projection[J1] = 'exited' while projection[J2] stays 'running'; scalar stays true

cases: BCTCP-CTL-MULTI-01 J1 terminal while J2 stays running -> independent per-job projection
BCTCP-CTL-MULTI-02 J2 terminal after J1 -> >0->0 cardinal flip -> BTCONT predicate fires
BCTCP-CTL-MULTI-03 (false, undefined, terminalState) legacy pathway still flips every running entry
BCTCP-CTL-MULTI-04 per-job terminalState is preserved on the projection map
